Not for outages happening now.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: user1\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  tier: \\\\\"aws-support-managed\\\\\"\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Explains and reduces Amazon Bedrock spend and checks capacity: pricing tiers, Provisioned Throughput, quotas and token drift.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"GENERIC\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon Bedrock, AWS Service Quotas, Amazon CloudWatch\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"AI/ML, Cost Optimization, Capacity Planning\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# OpsAI \\\\u2014 Capacity & Cost\\\\n\\\\nYou review Amazon Bedrock capacity and GenAI cost, read-only, with evidence for every number. Handle\\\\nout-of-scope areas (\\\\\"When NOT to Use\\\\\") with *Related skills (optional)*; never call another skill to do\\\\nthis one\\'s work.\\\\n\\\\n**Answer in this chat.** Run this skill\\'s read-only checks and answer here. Full method:\\\\n[cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) \\\\u00a71.\\\\n\\\\n**Billed spend** comes from `ce:GetCostAndUsage`:\\\\n- **Per model:** group by `PRODUCT_ATTRIBUTE` `model` (keys like `model$Claude Sonnet 5`; `model$` holds\\\\n  non-model costs) or by `USAGE_TYPE`. Group, don\\'t filter: product-attribute filters and\\\\n  `--dimension-key` are rejected.\\\\n- **Usage types** vary (`-mantle-`, `-standard`, `-flex`, `-priority`, `-cross-region-global`): match a\\\\n  model\\'s lines loosely. `-mantle-\\\\u2026-standard` bills at the Standard rate and does not mean the\\\\n  bedrock-mantle endpoint; that comes from `AWS/Bedrock` vs `AWS/BedrockMantle` metrics (api-quirks\\\\n  \\\\u00a720). `AWS/Bedrock` traffic through a `us.`/`eu.`/\\\\u2026 profile uses the `Cross-region \\\\u2026` quota.\\\\n- **No `SERVICE = \\\\\"Amazon Bedrock\\\\\"` filter:** Bedrock bills under several service names. Omit the\\\\n  filter, or list the names with `ce:GetDimensionValues` (`SERVICE`, search `Bedrock`).\\\\n- **Guardrail spend** (`USE1-Guardrail-*`, in `model$`) is a labelled line, not a finding.\\\\n- **Per caller or application** is billed only through IAM principal attribution (identity captured\\\\n  automatically; per-identity rows need a CUR 2.0 export with caller identity, tag dimensions need\\\\n  activated tags), application inference profiles, or Projects/Workspaces tags with activated cost\\\\n  allocation tags (cost-analysis \\\\u00a71a.5); otherwise it is an estimate.\\\\n\\\\n**Token model** (the cross-check; the result when Cost Explorer is denied or empty; per-caller splits;\\\\nwhat-ifs): price all four token types (`InputTokenCount`, `OutputTokenCount`,\\\\n`CacheReadInputTokenCount`, `CacheWriteInputTokenCount`) at their own rates and state the tier and\\\\nrouting (default Standard, source region).\\\\n- **Rates**, in order: the user (say so); `pricing:GetProducts` (us-east-1, one call per model; it does\\\\n  not use up `verify_aws_claim`\\'s single read) with service code `AmazonBedrockFoundationModels` for\\\\n  Claude and other third-party models, filters `regionCode` and `model` = the Pricing name (`Claude\\\\n  Sonnet 5`, `Claude Haiku 4.5`), and `AmazonBedrock` for Amazon models (an empty `AmazonBedrock`\\\\n  result for Claude does not mean unpriced); or the [pricing page](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/)\\\\n  read with `verify_aws_claim`. Denied: \\\\\"unpriced: pricing:GetProducts denied\\\\\".\\\\n- **Never** a rate from memory, a launch post or \\\\\"the same price as the previous generation\\\\\"; never\\\\n  back-derive a rate from the bill, or apply a bill-derived rate to $0-billed tokens or other days.\\\\n  No citable price: \\\\\"cross-check not computed\\\\\" and why.\\\\n- **What-if:** label it a what-if, not billed spend; a model switch needs a quality evaluation first\\\\n  (LLM-COST-004). Future volume goes to the AWS Pricing Calculator.\\\\n\\\\n**Pasted figures: re-read only billing days with a gap.** Run the re-read yourself in the connected\\\\naccount (Cost Explorer endpoint `us-east-1`); don\\'t ask for an account or Region first. A failed call:\\\\n\\\\\"not re-read: <error>\\\\\", then label that day from the pasted figures.\\\\n- **Today** (the current UTC day): no re-read; \\\\\"not billed yet\\\\\".\\\\n- **An earlier day with a gap** (fewer billed than metered tokens, or no line): re-read only those\\\\n  days on both sides, one `ce:GetCostAndUsage` (`DAILY`, by `SERVICE` and `USAGE_TYPE`) and one\\\\n  `cloudwatch:GetMetricData` (the user\\'s metric and `ModelId`, `Sum`, `Period` 86400). A pull made\\\\n  during a day is partial on both sides. If the re-read matches, stop: no metric listing, no scan of\\\\n  other usage types or services. Look further only if a gap remains (cost-analysis \\\\u00a71b).\\\\n- **Matching days, and pasted CloudWatch series and quotas on other days:** use as given, unless a\\\\n  value the answer needs is missing (e.g. `Maximum` where `Sum` is needed) or the user asks for\\\\n  current data.\\\\n\\\\nSay which figures you re-read and which came from the user.\\\\n\\\\n**Token reconciliation** needs no price, so it always runs: per UTC day, over the union of models with\\\\ntokens or a billed line, compare CloudWatch tokens with billed `UsageQuantity` (often in thousands)\\\\nand name the service of each usage type.\\\\n- Tokens with no billed line: \\\\\"metered, not billed \\\\u2014 unexplained\\\\\". A billed line with no tokens:\\\\n  \\\\\"billed, not metered\\\\\". Never drop either.\\\\n- Fewer billed than metered, labelled only from figures read now: today \\\\\"not billed yet\\\\\"; yesterday\\\\n  \\\\\"partly billed\\\\\" (both counts, kept out of the divergence, billed total not complete yet); 2 or\\\\n  more days old \\\\\"metered above billed \\\\u2014 unexplained\\\\\" (check cost-analysis \\\\u00a71b causes first). A\\\\n  re-read that matches is reported as matching.\\\\n- Quantity billed at $0.00: give the days, quantities and \\\\\"billed at $0 \\\\u2014 reason not visible from\\\\n  these reads\\\\\", and stop. Only a `RECORD_TYPE` line you read is a cause: no hypothesis, no \\\\\"most\\\\n  likely\\\\\". Point to the billing console or AWS Billing support; never re-price these tokens as owed.\\\\n- Never name a cause you haven\\'t checked (e.g. \\\\\"traffic outside the window\\\\\"): compare dates first.\\\\n\\\\n**Divergence:** compare modelled and billed per model and in total. Beyond a few percent, report it and\\\\nitemise what the token model doesn\\'t cover (PT model-unit hours, tier or routing suffixes, non-token\\\\nfeatures).\\\\n\\\\n## Router\\\\n\\\\nHow to read each API and metric: [collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md) (load\\\\nit with any row). If one read would answer the question, make it before answering; don\\'t end by\\\\noffering to pull it. The exception is the full quota sweep: ask for the code instead (Step 6).\\\\n\\\\n**Sub-agents** don\\'t see this skill. When you hand work to one, put in its task the rules its answer\\\\nmust follow: `(billed)` / `(estimated)` labels, the Cost Explorer service names read, where each\\\\nprice came from, `LLM-XXX-NNN (SEVERITY)` check-ids, no 12-digit numbers. Check its answer against\\\\n\\\\\"Rules for every answer\\\\\" before you reply, and fix what doesn\\'t hold.\\\\n\\\\n| Operator says | First read | Load |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| Why is my bill so high, spend by model | One `ce:GetCostAndUsage` over the window by `SERVICE` and `USAGE_TYPE` (per-model lines and service names in one read; add `PRODUCT_ATTRIBUTE` `model` only if a usage type doesn\\'t name the model), then `InputTokenCount`/`OutputTokenCount` by `ModelId` once for the cross-check | cost-analysis.md (LLM-COST-001) |\\\\n| Is my PT idle | `GetProvisionedModelThroughput` `modelUnits` vs token throughput | cost-analysis.md (LLM-PT-001) |\\\\n| Move to batch inference? | `Invocations` and the job\\'s latency tolerance | cost-analysis.md (LLM-COST-003) |\\\\n| Is a cheaper model enough? | `InvokeModel`/`Converse` `ModelId` vs task complexity and volume | cost-analysis.md (LLM-COST-004) |\\\\n| Runaway output, unbounded `maxTokens`? | `OutputTokenCount` (Sum) distribution per `ModelId` | cost-analysis.md (LLM-COST-001) |\\\\n| Same prompt prefix every call, is caching paying off? | `InputTokenCount` vs cache reads and writes | cost-analysis.md (LLM-COST-002) |\\\\n| Am I paying for cross-region inference? | Profile id prefix and source-region billing | cost-analysis.md (LLM-COST-005) |\\\\n| Throttled, enough quota? | `InvocationThrottles` (Sum), `EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage` (Sum, 60 s) vs the quota from `GetServiceQuota` | checks-model-invocation.md (LLM-INV-007, LLM-INV-002) |\\\\n| What is our limit, how do I find it? | Throttle data and peak now; code from quota-codes.md or the user, then `GetServiceQuota`; else ask for it (Step 6) | quota-codes.md, api-quirks.md \\\\u00a718 |\\\\n| Invocation logs growing forever | Log destination and its retention policy | metrics-and-logs.md (LLM-COST-006) |\\\\n| Alarms on token spend or quota | Recommended token, quota and throttle alarms | cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md |\\\\n\\\\n## Procedure \\\\u2014 Capacity & Cost Review\\\\n\\\\nRun the steps in order. Each step is bounded: a denied API, no datapoints or an unsupported region is recorded as `unavailable` /\\\\n`not checked` and the review goes on. A partial review with disclosed gaps is a correct result.\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: **Scope:** region(s), window, models and profiles; state the defaults chosen (current\\\\n  region, trailing window).\\\\n  - **Window:** Cost Explorer `End` and CloudWatch `EndTime` are exclusive: [`Start`, `End`) at 00:00\\\\n    UTC; to include day D set `End` = D + 1. Compute dates from today\\'s UTC date, never hardcode.\\\\n    Default `End` = today, so yesterday is the last day: mark it possibly incomplete, never drop it\\\\n    (api-quirks \\\\u00a722).\\\\n  - **Regions** are where requests are sent from. Cost Explorer is account-wide (read once, group by\\\\n    `REGION`); metrics, quotas, logging and PT are per region: run Steps 2, 2b, 5 and 6 in each.\\\\n    Profile traffic is recorded only in the source region (api-quirks \\\\u00a714).\\\\n  - **User-supplied evidence** is analysed as given. If live data differs, show both and say which\\\\n    each finding rests on.\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: **Tokens:** `InputTokenCount` and `OutputTokenCount` (Sum) from `AWS/Bedrock` by\\\\n  `ModelId`, same window as the cost data, 1-day period, days added (metrics-and-logs.md). Add every\\\\n  form of a model (short ID, profile ARN, model ARN). Billed spend with no tokens in the region: check\\\\n  another source region (the line\\'s `REGION` or usage-type prefix such as `USE1-`), the bedrock-mantle\\\\n  endpoint (`AWS/BedrockMantle` `TotalInputTokens`/`TotalOutputTokens` by `Model`, api-quirks \\\\u00a720),\\\\n  Batch (`AWS/Bedrock/Batch`) and PT (provisioned-model ARN). Name a cause only when a read shows it;\\\\n  otherwise \\\\\"billed, not metered\\\\\" and what you checked.\\\\n- [ ] Step 2b: **Confirming signals** for LLM-COST-001/002: cache read and write tokens (Sum, by\\\\n  `ModelId`); if a Bedrock invocation log group exists, the Logs Insights queries in\\\\n  metrics-and-logs.md (`stopReason`, `outputTokenCount` outliers, cache fields), even when\\\\n  `storedBytes` reads 0 (it lags), checking each field path with `ispresent()` first.\\\\n  - Same window as the cost data. Logs start at the group\\'s `creationTime`: disclose shorter\\\\n    coverage, never shorten the window (api-quirks \\\\u00a719). `StartQuery` takes epoch seconds: compute\\\\n    them with a tool.\\\\n  - LLM-COST-001 needs a heavy output tail of records stopped by `max_tokens` (long `tool_use` /\\\\n    `end_turn` outputs or a low uniform cap don\\'t count). LLM-COST-002 needs cache reads measured 0\\\\n    plus a repeated prefix or a high input floor (10th percentile, not the average). Otherwise\\\\n    `INFO (unconfirmed)`, with the missing signal disclosed (cost-analysis \\\\u00a71).\\\\n  - Counts and averages from one source and one window; never divide CloudWatch totals by log counts.\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: **Cost model** per \\\\\"Billed vs estimated cost\\\\\": billed per model, the four-token\\\\n  cross-check, daily reconciliation, divergence. Cost Explorer denied or empty: the token model is\\\\n  the result, `(estimated)`, with the missing billed cross-check disclosed.\\\\n- [ ] Step 3b: **Coverage check** (understating spend is the worst error). Pull daily billed cost and\\\\n  token Sums per model (all `ModelId` forms and `AWS/BedrockMantle`) up to today. If the first or\\\\n  last day, yesterday or today has cost or tokens, extend `End` and recompute, or report that day\\\\n  separately; if more than a few percent falls outside the window, report it and widen the window.\\\\n  Until this passes write \\\\\"within the window `<start>` \\\\u2192 `<end>` (exclusive)\\\\\"; if it can\\'t run, say\\\\n  the figure may understate spend, and why.\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: **COST checks** LLM-COST-001 to 006 (002 for every model with cache writes); decide\\\\n  003/004 from the invocation pattern and the stated workload, at catalog severity.\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: **Provisioned Throughput and reserved capacity** (cost-analysis \\\\u00a72): `modelUnits` vs\\\\n  observed throughput, and billed `\\\\u2026-reserved-\\\\u2026-tokens-per-minute` lines vs observed tokens per\\\\n  minute. Neither: \\\\\"no Provisioned Throughput or reserved capacity in `<region>`\\\\\", LLM-PT-001/003 not\\\\n  applicable, LLM-PT-002 still runs. PT can\\'t be resized in place (`UpdateProvisionedModelThroughput`\\\\n  changes only the name or model): give the LLM-PT-001 remediation, never an update command.\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: **Headroom and throttling** (api-quirks \\\\u00a717\\\\u201318).\\\\n  - **Pressure:** `InvocationThrottles` and `InvocationClientErrors` (Sum), per `ModelId` and with no\\\\n    dimension, per day. Count `ServiceQuotaExceededException` where invocation logs record it, else\\\\n    say client errors could not be split. LLM-INV-007 and LLM-PT-002 need throttles > 0 or confirmed\\\\n    quota rejections. Mantle rejections (HTTP 429) are not observable.\\\\n  - **LLM-INV-002:** a `ModelId` that `GetInferenceProfile` rejects is a direct call; raise only if\\\\n    `ListInferenceProfiles` has a profile for that model.\\\\n  - **Peak:** `EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage` (Sum, 60 s) over the trailing 15 days in one query per\\\\n    `ModelId`, max datapoint, never a single suspected day; forms sharing a quota are added minute by\\\\n    minute. If empty, re-check a day with traffic before \\\\\"no datapoints\\\\\". State statistic, period and\\\\n    window; the metric is an approximation. Give each peak its own timestamp: the token peak and the\\\\n    request peak can fall on different days.\\\\n  - **When to read the quota:** only if the user asks for the limit, headroom, an increase size or a\\\\n    percent-of-quota alarm, or throttles or quota rejections are above 0. Otherwise skip it and say\\\\n    \\\\\"headroom not computed: no throttles in the window and the limit wasn\\'t asked for\\\\\".\\\\n  - **Quota, read live** (api-quirks \\\\u00a718): headroom = peak \\\\u00f7 the applied TPM quota. Resolve the model\\\\n    and pick the form from how it is called. Take the code from the user, from earlier in this review,\\\\n    or from [quota-codes.md](references/quota-codes.md) (read it first): one `GetServiceQuota`, returned\\\\n    name checked. Never a remembered or guessed code.\\\\n    Without one, don\\'t sweep: `ListServiceQuotas` can\\'t filter by name (54 pages, 10+ minutes in\\\\n    testing). Answer with the throttle data and the peak, then ask for the code: name the exact quota\\\\n    (e.g. \\\\\"Cross-region model inference tokens per minute for Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5\\\\\") and give the\\\\n    console path (Service Quotas \\\\u2192 Amazon Bedrock, search that name) and the CLI command (\\\\u00a718 step 3).\\\\n    If the user mentions an earlier increase request, `list_requested_service_quota_change_history`\\\\n    (`ServiceCode=bedrock`) returns its code. Sweep only when the user asks for it (\\\\u00a718 step 3).\\\\n  - **Report** the rows read as a table: | Quota name | Code | Applied value | Adjustable |, one row\\\\n    per quota (`GetServiceQuota` or sweep). \\\\\"Not computed\\\\\" needs a named reason (code not given yet; rows in\\\\n    other forms only: name them; no TPM row: name the closest rows), then the raw peak. Pressure with\\\\n    high TPM headroom: check the RPM and daily quotas before naming a cause.\\\\n- [ ] Step 7: **Alarms** from [cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md](references/cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md),\\\\n  with each threshold\\'s source (AWS-published / Derived / Workload-specific).\\\\n- [ ] Step 8: Assemble the findings, then run \\\\\"Before You Present\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n## Check Families\\\\n\\\\nDetection rules, remediations, citations: [cost-analysis.md](references/cost-analysis.md) (PT, COST),\\\\n[checks-model-invocation.md](references/checks-model-invocation.md) (INV-002, INV-007). Check families\\\\nof other skills (GRD, KB, AGT, SM, EVAL, AC, TEL, other INV) are never raised here.\\\\n\\\\n| check-id | Detects | Severity |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| LLM-PT-001 | PT `InService` with sustained low use: no datapoints on most days, or throughput far below a known per-unit capacity (cost-analysis \\\\u00a72) | HIGH |\\\\n| LLM-PT-002 | On-demand load sustained near its throttle ceiling, no PT: a steady baseline cheaper or more reliable on PT | MEDIUM |\\\\n| LLM-PT-003 | PT on a model version nearing or past end of life | MEDIUM |\\\\n| LLM-COST-001 | A few invocations drive a large share of `OutputTokenCount`: unbounded `maxTokens`, spend drift | MEDIUM |\\\\n| LLM-COST-002 | Repeated prefixes with no prompt caching, or cache writes far above reads | MEDIUM |\\\\n| LLM-COST-003 | Large latency-tolerant jobs on-demand instead of Batch | MEDIUM |\\\\n| LLM-COST-004 | A high-cost model on simple high-volume tasks (validate a smaller one first) | MEDIUM |\\\\n| LLM-COST-005 | Cross-region profile with its billed rate unconfirmed (geographic: source-region rate; `global.`: a usage type containing `global`, own rate, documented at about 10% below geographic) | INFO |\\\\n| LLM-COST-006 | Invocation-log destination with no retention or lifecycle policy. Give `aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name <log-group> --retention-in-days <N>` (N workload-specific); data-delivery flags are configuration, out of scope here | MEDIUM |\\\\n| LLM-INV-002 | Direct model ID while a cross-region profile exists for that model (none: don\\'t raise) | HIGH |\\\\n| LLM-INV-007 | Sustained throttles or quota rejections (> 0) with no backoff retry and no profile spreading | MEDIUM |\\\\n\\\\n## Before You Present \\\\u2014 Validate Your Own Output\\\\n\\\\nA confidently wrong cost number is worse than a slow one. If an item can\\'t be met, say so.\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Every top rule and \\\\\"Guardrails \\\\u2014 details\\\\\" holds; no 12-digit number.\\\\n- [ ] Every dollar figure says `(billed)` or `(estimated)`, every finding `LLM-XXX-NNN (SEVERITY)`,\\\\n  billed spend names its Cost Explorer service names.\\\\n- [ ] Window stated with an exclusive `End`; Step 3b passed, or the figure is marked a possible\\\\n  understatement.\\\\n- [ ] No single SERVICE filter; the token model priced all four token types with tier and routing.\\\\n- [ ] Modelled vs billed per model and in total, or \\\\\"not computed\\\\\" and why; divergence itemised;\\\\n  partly billed days marked; each total equals the sum of its lines.\\\\n- [ ] Headroom = `EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage` \\\\u00f7 the TPM quota, code and name cited, quota rejections\\\\n  counted as pressure; every \\\\\"not computed\\\\\" has its reason; no code, no sweep: the code asked for.\\\\n- [ ] No cause and no \\\\\"should have cost\\\\\" figure for a $0 or gap day without a `RECORD_TYPE` line.\\\\n- [ ] Each check-id matches what was observed; {"id": "33266896-e107-489e-ae73-0165410558f4", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_AFz6NPxrKWxfBtr4xymZJq", "content": "[{'text': '# Cost Analysis\\n\\nBilled-vs-estimated cost methodology and cost-optimization checks for Bedrock + SageMaker GenAI workloads. This file carries the **COST** and **PT** (provisioned throughput) family checks.\\n\\nSeverity scale: CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW > INFO. Severity comes from each catalog row. A `workload-specific` threshold has no AWS-published value: name it as such next to the observed value, set it from observed usage, and keep the row\\'s severity.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. Cost methodology \u2014 billed first, token model second\\n\\nBedrock bills **four token types**, each at its own unit price: input, output, cache read, cache write. Unit prices also differ by **service tier** (Standard, Flex, Priority \u2014 where published) and by **routing** (in-region vs `cross-region-global`). Summing only input and output tokens at one rate per model is the most common cause of totals that do not match the bill. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-understanding-cur-data.html, https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/\\n\\n**1a. Billed spend (Cost Explorer = billed truth).** Label these figures `(billed)`.\\n1. **Per model:** `aws ce get-cost-and-usage --group-by Type=PRODUCT_ATTRIBUTE,Key=model --metrics UnblendedCost UsageQuantity` (also `provider`, `inferenceType`, `feature`). Results come back keyed by display name (`model$Claude Sonnet 5`, `model$Nova Lite`); `model$` holds costs with no model. With `GroupBy`, each period\\'s `Total` is empty (`{}`): read the `Groups`, never take the empty `Total` as $0; a period with no `Groups` has no billed spend in that grouping. `Type=DIMENSION,Key=model` fails with `ValidationException`; product-attribute filters and `--dimension-key` are rejected by current CLI/SDK builds, so group rather than filter. Product-attribute data starts at a fixed date. A window that begins earlier fails with `DataUnavailableException`. Don\\'t assume the date: on that error, regroup the same window by `USAGE_TYPE` and say so. API: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-cost-management/latest/APIReference/API_GetCostAndUsage.html\\n2. **Per usage type** (any period): group by `USAGE_TYPE`. Lines encode model, token type, tier and routing, but naming varies \u2014 e.g. `USE1-NovaLite-input-tokens` vs `USE1-anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-mantle-input-tokens-standard` \u2014 so match a model\\'s lines loosely. `UsageQuantity` is often in thousands of tokens. Provisioned Throughput bills as model-unit hours, not tokens.\\n3. **Guardrail spend** bills as `USE1-Guardrail-*` usage types and appears in the `model$` product-attribute group. Label it as Guardrail cost and treat Guardrail posture as out of scope (see *Related skills (optional)* in `SKILL.md`).\\n4. **Service name:** do not filter on `SERVICE = \"Amazon Bedrock\"`. Bedrock costs can appear under more than one service name, so a single-name filter undercounts (`api-quirks.md` \u00a716). Omit the SERVICE filter with product attributes, or list names with `ce:GetDimensionValues` (`Dimension = SERVICE`, `SearchString = Bedrock`).\\n5. **Per caller / per application** (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-management.html). Billed attribution exists in four forms, each aggregated per usage type per day in Cost Explorer and CUR 2.0 (never per request):\\n   - **IAM principal attribution** (bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle): the caller\\'s IAM user or role is captured automatically for every request, with no tags and no code change. A per-identity breakdown needs a **CUR 2.0 data export created with the caller-identity option**; an export created before that option was selected doesn\\'t include it. Team or cost-centre dimensions come from principal or session tags (`iamPrincipal/` prefix in CUR 2.0), which appear only after the principal\\'s first Bedrock call and must be activated as cost allocation tags (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-iam-principal-tracking.html).\\n   - **Application inference profiles** (bedrock-runtime): tags on the profile, activated as cost allocation tags.\\n   - **Projects** (bedrock-mantle Responses and Chat Completions) and **Workspaces** (bedrock-mantle Anthropic Messages): project resource tags, activated as cost allocation tags.\\n   Without one of these, a per-caller split is `(estimated)`. Before saying no billed per-team split exists, list application inference profiles (`bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles`, `typeEquals=APPLICATION`) and their tags, and name any you find.\\n   **Tag activation:** only the management (payer) account of an organization, or a standalone account, can use the cost allocation tags manager (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/custom-tags.html). A member account\\'s attempt returns `Cost allocation tags are managed at the payer account level` (IAM principal attribution page): that is expected, not a permission to add; say the management account activates the tag key. A new key can take up to 24 hours to appear for activation and up to 24 hours more to activate (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/activating-tags.html). Activation applies from then on; the management account can request a backfill of activation status for up to twelve months, and backfilled months carry tag values only where the resource already had the tag (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/cost-allocation-backfill.html).\\n\\n**1b. Token model (cross-check and fallback).** Label these figures `(estimated)`.\\n1. Pull `InputTokenCount`, `OutputTokenCount`, `CacheReadInputTokenCount`, `CacheWriteInputTokenCount` (Sum) from `AWS/Bedrock`, by `ModelId`, over the window.\\n2. Multiply each token type by its rate. Rate sources, in order: prices the user supplied (say so); `pricing:GetProducts`; the Bedrock pricing page (https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/) read with `verify_aws_claim`. `pricing:GetProducts` is an AWS API call, not a docs verification, so it doesn\\'t use up `verify_aws_claim`\\'s single read; the overview page often lacks per-model rates, so don\\'t spend that read on one model\\'s page per model. `GetProducts` (us-east-1 endpoint, one call per model): service code `AmazonBedrockFoundationModels` for third-party models or `AmazonBedrock` for Amazon models, filter `regionCode` plus `model` with the Pricing name (`Claude Sonnet 5`, `Nova Lite`, `Nova 2.0 Lite`) or, for Titan, `titanModel` (`TitanEmbeddingsV2-Text-input`). Read tier and routing from each row\\'s `usagetype` (contains `global` in any case = global; `flex`, `priority`; none = Standard) and skip rows containing `batch`, `custom-model`, `Customization`, `ProvisionedThroughput` or `reserved`. In testing, 5 calls priced all 5 models in use, Claude Sonnet 5 at $2.20/$11 per 1M (Standard), matching the bill. Match the exact model name and version as published (e.g. `Claude Sonnet 4.6`; `Claude Sonnet 5` \u2260 `Claude Sonnet 5.5`) and the region. Take the on-demand rate for the assumed tier (Standard, Flex, Priority) and routing (in-region, geographic, global); billed usage types show which apply (`-flex`, `-priority`, `-cross-region-global` / `_global_standard`; none of these = Standard). Billed `-mantle-\u2026-standard` lines bill at the model\\'s Standard rate (verified exact for Claude Sonnet 5). Don\\'t use batch, custom-model, Provisioned Throughput or reserved rates for on-demand tokens. Only published tiers exist (Nova Micro has Standard only). Read each rate\\'s unit (per 1K or per 1M tokens) and record the date the page was read. A rate no source gives = unpriced. Standard and global rates differ; CloudWatch tokens are split by neither, so state the rate you assumed. Never back-derive a rate from the bill for the cross-check \u2014 it matches by construction. With no citable price, write \"cross-check not computed\" with the reason; never drop the cross-check silently. You may still report the billed effective rate per usage-type line (`UnblendedCost` \u00f7 `UsageQuantity`) as an observation labelled \"derived from the bill, not a cross-check\". That rate describes only the days it was read from: never apply it to other days, other models or tokens billed at $0, and never use it to size what $0-billed usage \"would\" cost. If `pricing:GetProducts` is denied (AccessDenied: the managed `AIDevOpsAgentAccessPolicy` does not include it), report the model as \"unpriced: pricing:GetProducts denied\" and list the permission under scope not covered.\\n3. Compare CloudWatch token counts with billed `UsageQuantity` **per day** (`--granularity DAILY`, group by `USAGE_TYPE`) for every model with metered tokens, whether or not a price is citable. Report days or models with metered tokens and no billed line as \"metered, not billed \u2014 unexplained\"; check dates before naming a cause. Label a day with fewer billed than metered tokens only from figures read now (your own read, or a re-read on both sides of figures the user pasted, SKILL.md \"Pasted figures\"): the current UTC day is \"not billed yet\"; yesterday is \"partly billed\", because Cost Explorer lags CloudWatch: show both token counts, keep it out of the divergence, and say the billed total is not complete yet (in testing, a day\\'s billed tokens matched CloudWatch through 13:00 UTC; the evening\\'s traffic was still unbilled about 23 hours later). A day 2 or more days old with clearly more metered than billed tokens is \"metered above billed \u2014 unexplained\": give both counts and, before naming a cause, check that the day has stopped billing (a later read no longer changes it), that the metered side isn\\'t double-counted (`ModelId` + `ContextWindow` added to `ModelId`, metrics-and-logs.md) and the window and period (`api-quirks.md` \u00a721\u201322). In testing, a reported 2.1\u00d7 gap (9.0M metered vs 4.26M billed input) was a partly billed day plus today\\'s unbilled traffic. Then compare dollars per model and in total against 1a. A match only shows that the two sources agree inside the window. Before calling any figure exact or complete, run the coverage check (SKILL.md Step 3b, `api-quirks.md` \u00a722). `End` is exclusive, so check that no model has billed cost or tokens on days the window leaves out, in particular yesterday and today. If the gap is more than a few percent, report it and itemise the billed lines the model does not cover: PT model-unit hours, `-flex` / `-priority` / `-cross-region-global` lines priced differently from the assumed rate, and non-token features.\\n4. Use the token model as the result only when 1a is unavailable (Cost Explorer denied, or no data for the window), for per-caller or per-application allocation without billed attribution, and for what-if comparisons. Say which case applies.\\n\\nDirect any forward-looking price projections to the AWS Pricing Calculator / Bedrock pricing page \u2014 do not fabricate future prices.\\n\\n**Confirmation signals for LLM-COST-001 and LLM-COST-002.** Both checks describe a usage pattern that token totals alone cannot prove. Raise them at catalog severity only when one of these read-only signals confirms the pattern; otherwise raise `INFO (unconfirmed)` and name the missing signal:\\n\\n- `CacheReadInputTokenCount` / `CacheWriteInputTokenCount` (`AWS/Bedrock`, Sum, by `ModelId`). AWS documents that both are **0 when prompt caching is not used**, and that `InputTokenCount` excludes cached tokens. A *measured* 0 on cache reads confirms LLM-COST-002 only together with either (a) the prefix-hash query (metrics-and-logs.md) showing one prompt prefix on a large share of the model\\'s calls (state the share), or (b) a high input floor: the 10th percentile of `input.inputTokenCount`, not the average, at or above the model\\'s minimum tokens per cache checkpoint (512 to 4,096 depending on the model, e.g. 1,024 for Claude Sonnet 5 and 4,096 for Claude Haiku 4.5; read the exact value from the table on https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html). A low floor with a high average means mixed prompt sizes and confirms nothing on its own: raise `INFO (unconfirmed)`. In testing, Claude Sonnet 5 had cache reads 0, a minimum of 12, a 10th percentile of 1,936 and an average of 4,211 input tokens; one prefix hash covered 781 of 2,139 calls, which confirmed it through (a). *No datapoints* is not a 0 \u2014 it usually means the metric was not emitted (model may not support caching); report it as such (`api-quirks.md` \u00a715). Confirm the model supports prompt caching before raising. Amazon Nova models also cache implicitly, but that reuse isn\\'t reported in the cache fields and isn\\'t billed as cache reads (same page), so a Nova model\\'s cache reads of 0 say nothing about implicit reuse.\\n- **Caching in use but not paying off** (second form of LLM-COST-002): for every model with `CacheWriteInputTokenCount` > 0, compare it with `CacheReadInputTokenCount` (Sum, same window, by `ModelId`). Cache writes bill at the model\\'s cache-write rate, which for some models is higher than the standard input rate, and reads bill at the lower cache-read rate (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html), so caching saves money only when each written prefix is read back often enough to cover the write premium. Writes clearly above reads confirm this form: give both counts and the write:read ratio, and say the saving depends on the model\\'s write and read rates (price them per the token model, or say \"not priced\"). In testing, GPT-5.6 Terra wrote 4.4M and read 0.57M cache tokens in 14 days (7.7:1). Causes to check, not to assert: prefixes that change between calls, a cache TTL shorter than the gap between calls (the TTL resets on each hit and is model-specific: 5 minutes or 1 hour for current Claude models, 30 minutes for GPT-5.6 and GPT-6, 5 minutes for Nova), cache points on content that varies. Run this for every model in a cost review, not only when the user asks about caching.\\n- Invocation-log content (Logs Insights over the Bedrock log group): a `stopReason` shift toward `max_tokens` **together with** a heavy tail made of those `max_tokens` records (a small share of records carrying a disproportionate share of `outputTokenCount`) confirms LLM-COST-001. Neither of these confirms it: long outputs that stop on `tool_use` or `end_turn` (in testing, 97% of records stopped on `tool_use` and carried 99.7% of output), or a `max_tokens` share with uniformly small outputs (2.4% of records, all capped at 256 tokens). Raise `INFO (unconfirmed)`. Repeated identical prompt prefixes confirm LLM-COST-002.\\n\\n**Quota link.** Output tokens burn TPM quota at a model-specific burndown rate: on the `bedrock-runtime` endpoint AWS documents 2.5x for Claude Mythos 5/5.1/5.2, 5x for Claude Fable 5 and Anthropic models 4.7 and earlier, 10x for Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5.1/5.2 and OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, 15x for Claude 4.8, and 1:1 for every other model unless its model card says otherwise; `bedrock-mantle` models have separate input and output quotas and no burndown. Read the rate for the exact model from that page, never from memory. `max_tokens` is reserved from the quota up front for every request. An unbounded `maxTokens` therefore drives throttling (LLM-INV-007, LLM-PT-002) as well as cost \u2014 say so when both fire together. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-token-burndown.html\\n\\n| check-id | pillar | severity | detection-rule | remediation | AWS-doc-citation |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| LLM-COST-001 | Cost Optimization | MEDIUM | A small set of invocations drives a disproportionate share of `OutputTokenCount` (long generations) \u2014 unbounded `maxTokens`. Confirm only with a `max_tokens` shift **and** a heavy `outputTokenCount` tail made of `max_tokens` records; long `tool_use` / `end_turn` outputs, a low uniform cap, or no log signal raise `INFO (unconfirmed)`. | Cap `maxTokens`, add stop sequences, trim system prompts. Threshold `workload-specific`. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-parameters.html |\\n| LLM-COST-002 | Cost Optimization | MEDIUM | `CacheReadInputTokenCount` measured 0 together with a repeated prompt prefix (prefix-hash query) or a high input floor (10th percentile, not the average, at or above the model\\'s minimum cache-checkpoint size) \u2014 prompt caching not in use, inflating input-token cost; **or** `CacheWriteInputTokenCount` clearly above `CacheReadInputTokenCount` for a model \u2014 caching in use but rarely read back. Otherwise raise `INFO (unconfirmed)`. | Use prompt caching for stable prefixes where the model/API supports it; where writes exceed reads, make the cached prefix byte-identical across calls, match the cache TTL to the call spacing, or turn caching off for that path. Threshold `workload-specific`. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. Idle provisioned throughput detection (PT family)\\n\\nProvisioned Throughput (PT) buys dedicated model units billed hourly for the commitment term, regardless of use. Idle PT is pure waste.\\n\\nDetection: for each `GetProvisionedModelThroughput`, read `Invocations` and token Sums for the PT per UTC day over the window. Report observed tokens per minute next to the committed `modelUnits`, and the number of days with no datapoints; do not state a utilization % unless the user supplies the per-unit capacity (it varies by model). Using Anthropic Claude (char 28344-29735)\\n      - Using Amazon Nova (char 29736-30829)\\n    - Responses API (char 30830-34099)\\n    - Playground (char 34100-35648)\\n\\n# Prompt caching for faster model inference\\n\\nPrompt caching is an optional feature that you can use with supported models on Amazon Bedrock to\\nreduce inference response latency and input token costs. Amazon Bedrock supports two types of prompt\\ncaching: Implicit Prompt Caching and\\nExplicit Prompt Caching. Support for each\\ntype varies by model and API.\\n\\nPrompt caching can help when you have workloads with long and repeated contexts that are\\nfrequently reused for multiple queries. For example, if you have a chatbot where users can\\nupload documents and ask questions about them, it can be time consuming for the model to\\nprocess the document every time the user provides input. With prompt caching, you can cache\\nthe document so that future queries containing the document don't need to reprocess it.\\n\\n## Types of prompt caching\\n\\nThe two types differ in how reusable prompt content is selected:\\n\\n| Type | How it works | Request configuration |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Implicit Prompt Caching | Amazon Bedrock and the model automatically attempt to reuse eligible prompt prefixes. | No cache controls or breakpoints are required in your request. |\\n| Explicit Prompt Caching | You opt in by adding model-specific cache controls or breakpoints. | Your request must include the cache controls supported by the model and API. |\\n\\n### Implicit Prompt Caching\\n\\nImplicit Prompt Caching automatically attempts to reuse eligible prompt prefixes\\nwithout requiring cache controls in your request. Keep static content at the\\nbeginning of your prompt and dynamic content at the end to increase the likelihood\\nof an exact prefix match.\\n\\nImplicit Prompt Caching is best effort. Repeating an identical prompt doesn't\\nguarantee a cache hit, and cache-hit rates can vary.\\n\\n### Explicit Prompt Caching\\n\\nExplicit Prompt Caching lets you opt in to caching with\\nmodel-specific cache controls or *cache\\ncheckpoints*. Cache checkpoints are markers that define the\\ncontiguous subsection of your prompt that you want to cache. Prompt prefixes should\\nremain static between requests. Changes to a prompt prefix in subsequent requests\\nresult in cache misses.\\n\\nCache checkpoints have a minimum and maximum number of tokens, depending on the\\nmodel. You can only create a cache checkpoint if your total prompt prefix meets the\\nminimum number of tokens. Minimums currently range from 512 to 4,096 tokens per\\ncache checkpoint. For the minimum that applies to your model, see\\nSupported models, Regions, and explicit caching limits or the\\nmodel's model card. The minimum applies cumulatively to the entire\\nprompt prefix before each checkpoint, including, where applicable, content in the\\n`tools`, `system`, and `messages` fields. There\\nis no minimum number of tokens required between cache checkpoints. For a model with\\na 1,024-token minimum, you can define additional checkpoints fewer than 1,024 tokens\\napart as long as the total prompt prefix before each checkpoint contains at least\\n1,024 tokens. If you add a cache checkpoint before the total prompt prefix meets the\\nminimum number of tokens, your inference still succeeds, but your prefix isn't\\ncached.\\n\\nThe cache has a Time To Live (TTL), which resets with each successful cache hit.\\nDuring this period, the context in the cache is preserved. If no cache hits occur\\nwithin the TTL window, your cache expires. Many models support a 5-minute TTL.\\nCheck the model card for your model to see the exact TTL conditions.\\n\\nExplicit Prompt Caching provides control over which prompt content is eligible\\nfor caching. It doesn't guarantee that an eligible request results in a cache\\nhit. A cache entry is stored on the server that processed the request, and a later\\nrequest can read it only if that server handles it before the entry expires.\\nRequests that are served by a different server, such as one in another Region, or\\nthat are sent before an identical request has started its response, write a new\\nentry instead of reading one.\\n\\n### Billing for cached tokens\\n\\nFor both Implicit Prompt Caching and Explicit Prompt Caching, input tokens are\\nbilled at one of three rates. Tokens written to the cache are billed at the model's\\ncache-write rate, which, depending on the model, can be higher than the standard\\ninput token rate. Tokens read from the cache are reported as cached tokens and\\nbilled at the model's cache-read rate. All other input tokens are billed at the\\nstandard input token rate. Implicit cache reuse on Amazon Nova models is an exception;\\nsee Supported models, Regions, and explicit caching limits.\\nFor more information, see the\\nAmazon Bedrock pricing page.\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\nSupport for prompt caching doesn't guarantee a cache hit for any request. Check\\nthe cache usage fields in the model response to determine whether tokens were read\\nfrom or written to cache.\\n\\nYou can use prompt caching when you run inference in Amazon Bedrock with supported models.\\nAvailability of each prompt caching type varies by model and API. Prompt caching is\\navailable through the following Amazon Bedrock features:\\n\\n**Converse and ConverseStream APIs**\\n:   You can carry on a conversation with a supported model. For Explicit\\n    Prompt Caching, specify cache checkpoints in your prompts.\\n\\n**InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream APIs**\\n:   You can submit single-prompt requests to supported models. For Explicit\\n    Prompt Caching, enable prompt caching and specify your cache\\n    checkpoints.\\n\\n**Prompt Caching with Cross-region Inference**\\n:   Prompt caching can be used in conjunction with cross region inference. Cross-region\\n    inference automatically selects the optimal AWS Region from the Regions in your inference profile to\\n    serve your inference request, thereby maximizing available resources and model\\n    availability. At times of high demand, these optimizations may lead to increased cache writes.\\n\\n**Amazon Bedrock Prompt management**\\n:   When you create or modify a prompt, you can\\n    choose to enable prompt caching. Depending on the model, you can cache\\n    system prompts, system instructions, and messages (user and assistant). You\\n    can also choose to disable prompt caching.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nPrompt caching is only supported for on-demand inference endpoints. It is not supported with the batch inference API.\\n\\nFor models that support Explicit Prompt Caching, the APIs provide granular control\\nover the prompt cache. You can set individual cache checkpoints within your prompts\\nand add checkpoints up to the maximum allowed for the model. I checked the 14 days from 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-23, including today, which is only partly counted. I used CloudWatch token and cache metrics, Bedrock invocation logs (about 8,700 records, which cover the whole window), Cost Explorer under the `Amazon Bedrock` and `Amazon Bedrock Service` service names, and list prices.

### Claude Sonnet 5 (`us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`): LLM-COST-002 (MEDIUM)
- **Volume:** about 29.5M input tokens across 7,647 logged calls.
- **No caching:** cache reads and cache writes are both 0 on all 7,647 calls. The log fields are present, so these are measured zeros, not missing data.
- **Repeated prefixes:** six system-prompt prefixes cover about 84.5% of calls (6,460 of 7,647). The top one alone covers 25.3% (1,933 calls). This hash covers only the first 2,000 characters of the system prompt, so it shows the opening text repeats, not that the whole prefix matches.
- **Prompts are long enough:** the 10th-percentile input is about 1,827 tokens. The documented minimum per cache checkpoint for Sonnet 5 is 1,024, and it supports 5-minute and 1-hour TTLs.
- **Unit prices (list, us-east-1, Standard):** plain input is $2.20 per 1M tokens. A cache read is $0.22 (90% less). A cache write is $2.75, which is 25% more than plain input. A written prefix pays for itself after roughly one read inside the TTL.
- **Fix:** add cache checkpoints to the stable system and tools content. Keep the volatile content at the end of the prompt.

- **Writes with no reads:** 411,705 tokens written to the cache and 0 read, across 390 calls on 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-17. CloudWatch and the logs agree on both figures, and billing shows cache-write lines but no cache-read line.

- **Other models:** Sonnet 4.5 (133 input tokens), Nova Lite, Haiku 4.5, Llama and Titan have negligible volume or no caching signal, so I raised nothing for them.
